title: Decision Reviews and Appeals: Several Open Reviews and One Open Lane per Issue
content:
**Contact center desk guidance — Decision Reviews and Appeals**

**The rule.** A claimant may have several reviews open at once in Decision Reviews and Appeals, on different issues and in different lanes, with no limit on the number; each issue of a decision may be placed in its own lane. One issue is never pending in two lanes at the same time: a review is recorded only when no review of the same issue of the same decision is submitted or pending.

**What the rule turns on**

- *Number of open reviews.* There is no limit on how many reviews one claimant may have open.
- *Same issue of the same decision.* Two reviews concern the same issue of the same decision when they name the same decision under review and the same issue contested. Both must match. A review in a different lane on that same issue of that same decision is still a review of the same issue; choosing another lane does not make it a different issue.
- *Open status.* A review counts against a new request while its status is submitted (the request has been received but not yet established in its lane) or pending (it has been established in its lane, or docketed at the Board). A review that is decided or withdrawn is not submitted or pending.
- *Source of the facts.* Whether such a review exists is read from VA's own review records for the claimant, before the new review is recorded, matched on the decision under review and the issue contested.

**Condition — judgement — result**

| Existing review on the claimant's record | Its status | What this rule provides for the new request |
|---|---|---|
| Same decision, same issue | Submitted | Not recorded |
| Same decision, same issue | Pending | Not recorded |
| Same decision, same issue | Decided | This rule places no bar |
| Same decision, same issue | Withdrawn | This rule places no bar |
| Same decision, a different issue | Submitted or pending | This rule places no bar |
| A different decision, an issue of the same name | Submitted or pending | This rule places no bar |
| No existing review | — | This rule places no bar |

**Worked illustrations (hypothetical)**

1. A hypothetical rating decision decides two issues, hearing loss and tinnitus. The claimant has a Higher-Level Review pending on hearing loss and asks for a Board Appeal - Evidence Submission Docket review of tinnitus. The tinnitus request concerns a different issue of the decision, so this rule places no bar on it, and the claimant would then hold two open reviews in two lanes.
2. In the same hypothetical, the claimant also asks for a Supplemental Claim on hearing loss while the Higher-Level Review of hearing loss is still pending. The same issue of the same decision has a pending review, so the Supplemental Claim is not recorded.
3. Once that Higher-Level Review of hearing loss is decided, no review of that issue of that decision is submitted or pending, and this rule no longer stands in the way of a new request on it.
